The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: A software update changed the format of a saved summary of each shopper's spending, and the older version, still running beside the new one because the update stopped partway, could not read the new format and failed the account page.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 24.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 3,022.30 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while io-shop ran 696c33a
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 12:17 to 12:25 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 12:30 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 12:24:02 UTC
Ended by: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 12:17 UTC and was back to normal at 12:25 UTC, 8 minutes later. 17.7% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 24.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 3,022.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. A software update changed the format of a saved summary of each shopper's spending, and the older version, still running beside the new one because the update stopped partway, could not read the new format and failed the account page. What Argus did: rolled back the deployment of io-shop (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Code-Fix kept none of the fix it wrote, which helps only once code outside the repository changes as well: writing it again is AI-2. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). Account pages could fail again if revision 696c33a goes out again while the earlier revision is still serving, or if cache entries in its new format are left where the earlier revision reads.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
24.5% - peak error rate
1,698 - requests failed
1.0% to 17.7% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
3,022.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The new revision changed what a summary cache entry holds. It used to be a bare cents figure and is now 'amount/items' text (`_ENTRY_FORMAT`). The replicas still running the earlier revision read those same entries and raised ValueError on the new text in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py instead of treating it as a miss, so the account page request failed.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's share of failed requests rose well above its usual level.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 occurrences in 38 minutes, 11:47–12:24; # was 0.50% to 24.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 12:18
    G3714 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ValueError: summary cache entry '2400/8' is not a figure in cents at src/io_shop/summary_cache.py - 15 occurrences in 8 minutes, 12:17–12:24
why 1 The failing account page requests raised ValueError when they read a summary cache entry, '2400/8', that was not a figure in cents, in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py.
  Evidence:
    G3714
    Gc956 ERROR io-shop: summary cache entry could not be read - ValueError: summary cache entry '2400/8' is not a figure in cents at src/io_shop/summary_cache.py (# of 200 requests) - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 12:17–12:24; # was 15 to 48, typically 38, highest at 12:18
why 2 The cache held entries in the new 'amount/items' text format that revision 696c33a introduced, and the replicas reading them expected a bare cents figure. The new revision's own reader returns no error on text it cannot read, so the error comes from the reader in the earlier revision.
  Evidence:
    D1 Deployment of revision 696c33a to io-shop, compared against 5470c1a - the revision deployed before it.
    Gc956
    G3714
why 3 Deploy P2 at 12:17:36 UTC rolled out revision 696c33a, which brought in the new entry format. As of 12:24:10 UTC, its rolling update was paused partway, with replicas on 696c33a and on 5470c1a both serving against the same cache.
  Evidence:
    P2 12:17:36 UTC deploy 696c33a by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    T9 12:24:10 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - 3 of 6 replicas run revision 696c33a, deployed at 12:17:36, and 3 still run revision 5470c1a, of a deployment sized for 3; its rolling update is paused
    D1
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy P1 of revision 5470c1a: the service was measured healthy with it in place. The metrics read before the onset showed the usual error rate, account pages rendered normally before the onset, and the service returned to normal after the confirmed rollback left 5470c1a running.
      T4 12:24:06 Investigator Agent: Read back 361 minutes of metrics
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 5 occurrences in 26 minutes, 11:49–12:14
      M1 12:24:26 Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1: confirmed, still in place
      T19 12:26:04 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 12:25
      T20 12:26:04 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 12:24:21.
      T15
why 4 The new revision changed the format of cache entries that the still-serving older replicas also read, and the older revision's reader raised an error on the new format instead of treating it as a miss.
  Evidence:
    D1
    G3714
    Gc956
Contributing factors
- No check was seen, before the change went out, that the revision already serving could read cache entries in the new revision's format. (AI-4)
- No automatic rollout analysis was seen that halted or reverted io-shop's rolling update when its error rate rose. The rollout stayed partway, with both revisions serving. (AI-5)
- The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The rollout of revision 696c33a, deployed 12:17:36 UTC, stopped part way and is paused with 3 of 6 replicas on the new revision and 3 on 5470c1a.... The new revision writes summary cache entries as 'amount/items' text, such as '2400/8'. The old replicas still expect a bare cents figure and raise ValueError on those entries, which failed account pages from 12:17 UTC. | 0.88 | confirmed
C2 | The revision 696c33a has a code bug in how summary cache entries are written and read. This would matter only if the rollout had converged, which it has not. | 0.08 | confirmed, as tested for C1

Trigger
io-shop was deployed from 5470c1a to 696c33a at 12:17:36 UTC, by kuki.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 12:24:26 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 12:17 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 12:24 UTC, 7 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Write the fix again: its change to the repository and the change outside the repository that Code-Fix's reading names, made together - Code-Fix kept none of the fix it wrote | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a pre-deploy check, for every change to the format of a cached or stored entry, that runs the serving revision's reader against entries written in the candidate revision's format. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Add automated rollout analysis to io-shop's rolling updates that halts and reverts the rollout when the error rate rises while revisions are mixed. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came 6 minutes after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
- 10 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - 3 of 6 replicas run revision 696c33a, deployed at 12:17:36, and 3 still run revision 5470c1a, of a deployment sized for 3; its rolling update is paused.
- 21 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 12:24:21.
- 26 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
- 2 minutes 4 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- Code-Fix wrote a fix and said plainly that it helps only together with a change outside the repository, so no partial fix was kept.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Response effort

Supporting information

  +    """What the cache holds for one shopper: the figure, and what it covers.
  +
  +    A value rather than a bare figure, because the two are only a summary

  +    many purchases, and an entry carrying the first alone leaves the page

  +    entry goes in under the shopper it belongs to and comes back as the same

  +    """

  +    items_counted: int

  +        )

  +    entry has is text this revision has nothing to do with, and passing over it

  +    module fails no page - see the docstring at the top - and an entry that
  +    cannot be read is, to the page in front of it, an entry that is not there.
  +    """
  +    amount, separator, items = written.partition(_ENTRY_SEPARATOR)
  +
  +    if not separator:
  +        return None
  +
  +    try:
  +        return SummaryEntry(amount_cents=int(amount), items_counted=int(items))
  +    except ValueError:

... and the changes to 2 more files, not shown: the diffs above reached the 200 lines one answer carries. Those files are named above; what changed inside them is not here.
What Code-Fix read in the source - nothing ran to check it
F1 | Yes. Old replicas crash on '2400/8' because something writes str(SummaryEntry) under the bare shopper id, which is where revision 5470c1a reads. That writer isn't in this repository: the cache is reached only through a LookUpSummary seam the deployment supplies, and no code here writes entries. My patch only moves where this revision reads, to summary_key_for(shopper_id) = summary:v2:<shopper_id>. On its own, that leaves the new-format text under the bare key and the old replicas still failing on it. For the change to help, the writer outside this repo must store new-format entries under summary_key_for(shopper_id) and never under the bare shopper id. It must also stop writing that shape at the old address while any 5470c1a replica is still serving. Any '/'-format entries already sitting under bare shopper ids need deleting or expiring before the rollout resumes.
How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main
U1 | cached_summary at src/io_shop/account_page.py:237, in _the_figure_for: calls it: found = cached_summary(account.shopper_id, look_up_summary, cache_endpoint)

- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-11
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not load their account pages, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. A software update changed the format of a saved summary of each shopper's spending. The update stopped partway, so the older version kept running beside the new one. The older version could not read the new format, and account pages it served failed. Argus estimates the lost takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, so no one had to respond out of hours. Argus ended the incident by rolling back the io-shop deployment and confirmed that it worked. The rollback is still in place, and automatic sync has been left off.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
